title: The heat of Tabuk
hookLine: in the heat before Tabuk, Uthman equips the army, and Abu Dharr walks alone behind it

lines: DON'T GO OUT IN THIS HEAT.
cards: Summer in Medina. Ka'b ibn Malik, in Sahih al-Bukhari, remembers the fruit ripe and the shade inviting. And the call goes out to march north toward Tabuk, a long way through hard heat.

The Qur'an itself records what those who stayed behind said: don't go out in this heat. It answers them that the fire of hell is fiercer in heat, if only they understood. That's surah nine, al-Tawbah.
The army that gathers has a name in the hadith: the army of hardship. Today: the heat of Tabuk.

teach.b: Two people stand out in this march. The first is Uthman ibn Affan. When the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, asks who will equip the army of hardship, Sahih al-Bukhari reports that Uthman did it.
The collection of al-Tirmidhi adds a scene: Uthman pours coins into the Prophet's lap, and the Prophet turns them over in his hands and says that nothing Uthman does after this day will harm him.
A generous man, giving from plenty, at the moment it counts. The second is Abu Dharr.

The sirah of Ibn Ishaq tells that his camel is too slow and weak to keep up. He falls behind. So he takes his things off the camel, puts them on his own back, and walks, following the army's tracks through the heat.
Later, in camp, someone sees a lone figure coming along the road. The Prophet says: let it be Abu Dharr. And it is.

Then he says words about Abu Dharr that the sirah remembers: may Allah have mercy on him, he walks alone, he will die alone, and he will be raised alone. Put the two side by side. One gives a fortune.
One gives his own two feet.
Neither one waits for the conditions to be good. Uthman doesn't wait until giving is easy. Abu Dharr doesn't wait for a better camel.
And the Prophet sees both of them, the man with the coins in his lap and the man too far back for anyone else to notice.

how: Muslims retell the campaign of Tabuk from the Qur'an's ninth surah, the hadith collections and the sirah, and Uthman's gift and Abu Dharr's walk are told as two pictures of giving in hardship.

o: the hard summer march of the army of hardship
a winter camp where the army waited out the cold
a well where pilgrims rest on the road to Mecca

games.q: the heat of Tabuk — tap the pairs.
p: carried his load on his back
don't go out in this heat
the Prophet, seeing a lone figure

s: the march to Tabuk was in a cool season
it was summer heat, and those who stayed behind said: don't go out in this heat.
Abu Dharr waited in Medina for a better camel
he took his load on his back and walked after the army.
the army had a name in the hadith: the army of hardship

games.q: you're Abu Dharr. your camel can't keep up, and the army is out of sight. what do you do?
o: wait for someone to come for you.
load your things on your back and walk after them.
games.why: he walked alone in the army's tracks, and the Prophet, seeing a lone figure, said: let it be Abu Dharr.

practice: Bring to mind one shared thing that needs help, a mosque, a food bank, a school fund, a neighbor's repair, and if a voice says later, when things are easier, notice it.
Then ask which kind of giving fits you: Uthman's, from what you have, or Abu Dharr's, your own time and effort, carried on your back. If you pray, you can ask Allah to accept it.

wordCard.voice: Tabuk, the hard summer march where Uthman equipped the army of hardship and Abu Dharr, his camel failing, walked alone behind it. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'the army of hardship', the name the hadith gives the Tabuk army.

carryVoice: Your line: alone, walking behind. A fortune and two feet, both seen. Day seven hundred ninety-three.
